title: Why Your Mind Wanders
desc: You reach the bottom of a page and realize you haven't taken in a word. Where did your mind go, and is it a flaw or a feature? In this calm, sourced, sleep-friendly deep dive, we follow one imagined man, Anton, through a quiet evening, and ask why minds wander so often. Along the way we look at how scientists catch a wandering thought, a famous phone-app study of about 2,250 people, the brain's default mode network, what happens in the eyes and brain when we zone out while reading, where thoughts go (so often into the future), who wanders most, what it costs us in lectures and reading, why attention fades after about half an hour, what a wandering mind gives us in creativity and on a walk, Jerome Singer's styles of daydreaming, rumination and worry, mind-pops and uninvited thoughts, what happens when people are left alone with their thoughts, dreaming as mind wandering, what helps at bedtime, how green places restore attention, and mindfulness. We finish with a few gentle, research-based ideas and then a long, slow guided wind-down to help you fall asleep.
